results.title: Supreme Court won’t settle a debate through constitutional interpretation – Kwaku Azar on NPP presidential term limit suit
results.content: Legal scholar Kwaku Azar Asare has questioned whether the New Patriotic Party’s (NPP) suit at the Supreme Court seeking an interpretation of the presidential term limit presents a justiciable constitutional dispute or amounts to a request for an advisory opinion. The NPP has filed a suit at the Supreme Court seeking an interpretation of Article 66(2) of the 1992 Constitution, which provides for a presidential term of four years and limits a person to two terms in office. The party is seeking a declaration that the two-term limit applies whether the terms are consecutive or non-consecutive. The action has drawn attention to the constitutional implications of presidential term limits ahead of the 2028 general election. However, the filing of the suit does not, in itself, establish that President John Dramani Mahama intends to seek another term.

results.title: Kufuor condemns vote buying, says it undermines voters’ dignity
results.content: Former President John Agyekum Kufuor has condemned vote buying, warning that politicians who pay for votes undermine the dignity of citizens and risk treating the electorate as people they have purchased. He has urged political leaders to respect voters’ rights and recognise that electoral victory comes with a responsibility to serve and remain accountable to the people. Speaking in an interview with Evans Mensah on JoyNews’ PM Express, Mr Kufuor said any government that disregards the rights and dignity of citizens betrays the trust placed in it. “The humanity of each and every one of us is captured in this land. Any government that would come and look down upon any of us like people that should not be accorded the rights and entitlements as owners of this land, that government is a traitor. It has betrayed us,” he said.

results.title: Kufuor blames vanity and vindictiveness for Ghana’s poor policy continuity
results.content: Former President John Agyekum Kufuor has blamed vanity, vindictiveness and a lack of vision among successive governments for Ghana’s failure to sustain some of the socio-economic initiatives introduced by previous administrations. He said the tendency of incoming governments to abandon policies and agreements initiated by their predecessors had undermined opportunities for investment, institutional development and long-term national progress. Speaking in an interview with Evans Mensah on JoyNews’ PM Express, Mr Kufuor cited the cancellation of an agreement his administration negotiated with Barclays International as an example of what he described as a failure to appreciate the long-term benefits of policy continuity.

results.title: Government, organised labour sign 2-year public service remuneration agreement for 2027-2028

results.title: Spiritual Science Society donates supplies to Koforidua Prison
results.content: The Director-General of the Spiritual Science Society and SS Consultancy Services, Lord Ackkham Rebakham, has donated foodstuffs, toiletries and drinking water to support the welfare of inmates at the Koforidua Prison. The donation is intended to help meet the daily needs of inmates and ease some of the operational challenges facing the facility. Presenting the items, Lord Rebakham emphasised the importance of compassion and corporate social responsibility, saying society had a role to play in supporting people in custody. He said adequate support and rehabilitation were essential to helping inmates prepare for their eventual reintegration into society.
